dashboard_trackers.notes: UN reporting on deadly Russian attacks and aid-warehouse damage remains the newest authoritative update. A newly indexed Guardian item concerned earlier Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian warehouses, not a fresh 21 July strike cluster; the realized-war lane remains at 99%

dashboard_trackers.name: RUSSIA-NATO
dashboard_trackers.notes: NATO still lists Ukraine’s 20 July request through its civilian emergency-response mechanism as the only new dated operational item. No collective-defence step, allied combat entry, force movement against Russia or revised official nuclear-use threshold was identified

dashboard_trackers.name: CHINA-TAIWAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Newly indexed Taiwan reports continue to describe June Chinese government-vessel activity and blockade-rehearsal concerns, not a current PLA attack, quarantine declaration or live force concentration crossing the action threshold

dashboard_trackers.name: DPRK
dashboard_trackers.notes: Pyongyang’s threat of unspecified countermeasures over allied naval drills remains the latest development; no fresh launch event or nuclear detonation surfaced

dashboard_trackers.name: SUDAN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Fresh drone-war analysis and sanctions coverage did not establish a distinct same-day SAF-RSF offensive, new chemical deployment or Red Sea spillover. The already-extreme lane holds at 90%

dashboard_trackers.name: ISRAEL PALESTINE
dashboard_trackers.notes: The National reports residents fled renewed fire in eastern Gaza and says Israeli forces moved about 300 metres beyond the yellow line; Gaza health authorities report 1,158 deaths since the October truce. The cumulative toll is not independently verified in this scan, and the already near-ceiling lane holds at 88%

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH SUDAN ABYEI
dashboard_trackers.notes: No fresh confirmed Abyei or Uganda-South Sudan border attack surfaced. Current risk still rests on the previously corroborated Kajo-Keji skirmish, reinforcement and displacement evidence

dashboard_trackers.name: EASTERN DRC
dashboard_trackers.notes: OCHA’s daily humanitarian brief and a new analytical article produced no distinct same-day FARDC-M23 or Rwanda-linked battlefield escalation, so the lane holds at 52%

dashboard_trackers.name: YEMEN RED SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: The National cites Kpler data showing Saudi Red Sea crude loadings fell 36% over the two weeks ending 13 July, evidence of material route stress. The data predate the new Houthi embargo declaration, and the article says practical enforcement remains unclear; no attributable new vessel interdiction or Saudi strike followed, so risk holds at 46%

dashboard_trackers.name: MALI SAHEL
dashboard_trackers.notes: Follow-on reports continue to corroborate the heavy Anefis-Gao convoy losses, but no new strategic seizure, distinct mass-casualty event or regional-force intervention appeared after the already-scored attack cycle

dashboard_trackers.name: SOUTH CHINA SEA
dashboard_trackers.notes: AFP and France 24 report the U.S. State Department condemned China’s actions after the Second Thomas Shoal clash, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio reaffirmed the U.S. defensive umbrella on arrival in Manila. Canonical external backing is activated; absent firearms, death, vessel seizure or a new deployment, raw risk rises conservatively from 18% to 21%

dashboard_trackers.name: SOMALIA GULF OF ADEN
dashboard_trackers.notes: Al Jazeera, Marine Insight and Shipping Telegraph now corroborate the Asana tanker hijack and continuing pirate presence. Al Jazeera cites the Mica Center recording 18 piracy incidents since April and at least three other vessels still held; the three-mention/two-source gate is met and the new lane opens conservatively at 28%
